land.text: Hunza and Nagar, which 'acceded to Pakistan' in November 1947

successors.note: Hunza on 3 November, Nagar on 18 November 1947 (Gilgit-Baltistan page); both survived as princely states inside Pakistan, Nagar to August 1972 and Hunza to September 1974, and are not drawn apart.

capitals.name: Baltit (Karimabad)
capitals.note: Hunza page: 'The state capital was Baltit'; an earlier fort, Altit Fort, is mentioned without dates. Nagar's own seat was 'the town of Nagar' (Nagar page; infobox 'Nagarkhas'). The page gives no years and no coordinates: the span is the state's, the coordinates are approximate (the gazetteer has no Baltit/Karimabad entry).

correction.text: Hunza, 'an independent principality, established in around 1200'; the disc is the area of the infobox's 3,900 sq mi (10,000 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). Infobox area 10,000 km2; a 56 km disc is 9,850 km2 (ratio 0.99). The page gives no boundary; the centre is the point the Kashmir and British Raj dossiers use for the two valleys (74.7 E, 36.35 N).

correction.text: Hunza and Nagar together: 'Nagar was established in the 14th century and existed as an autonomous principality'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox areas: Hunza 10,000 km2, Nagar 4,100 km2, 14,100 km2 together; the 70 km disc is 13,400 km2 (53 cells; ratio 0.95), the region the Kashmir and British Raj ledgers use for their 1891 vassal_start. The two states are separate on the pages; one disc stands for both because no page gives the line between them.

ledger.note: c. 1200: the principality of Hunza is established. 'Hunza was an independent principality, established in around 1200'; infobox 'Established: c. 1200'. The page gives the year loosely and no boundary; the disc is the infobox's 10,000 km2.

region.text: Nagar, the neighbouring principality on the other bank, 'established in the 14th century'

ledger.note: c. 1300: Nagar appears beside Hunza. 'Nagar was established in the 14th century and existed as an autonomous principality' (infobox 'Established: c. 1300'); the pair is drawn as one state. The page says the early rulers' details are uncertain and the first definite dates are from 1839.

region.text: Hunza and Nagar, which acceded to Pakistan

ledger.note: November 1947: Hunza and Nagar accede to Pakistan. 'Hunza acceded to Pakistan on 3 November, followed by Nagar on 18 November.' The Hunza page quotes the Mir's telegram of 3 November 1947; the Nagar page says only 'In November 1947 ... acceded his state to the Dominion of Pakistan'. The states lasted inside Pakistan to 1972 (Nagar) and September 1974 (Hunza).

wars.name: Hunza-Nagar Campaign
wars.outcome: British victory: Hunza captured 22 December and the Baltit Fort and Nagar on 23 December 1891; Nazim Khan and Zafar Khan installed as the new rulers of Hunza and Nagar; the column was back in Gilgit on 11 January 1892.
wars.note: The campaign page lists only the British Raj against Hunza and Nagar (Kashmiri troops serve in the text). The 1891 vassal_start events (British Raj, Kashmir and Jammu) are recorded in those dossiers, which cite the Gilgit Agency page: 'both states were again subjugated by Anglo-Dogra forces in 1891'. The Gilgit-Baltistan page puts them 'under British suzerainty' and is silent on Kashmir's; the Nagar page has annual tribute to the Kashmir Durbar 'until 1947'.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a frontier of either state or a line between them; one 70 km disc stands for both. The valleys are mountain terrain and the borders were never surveyed in this period.

sources.title: Hunza (princely state)
sources.note: Identity, infobox c. 1200 to 1974, 10,000 km2, Baltit, tribute to China (from c. 1760) and the Dogras (1860), 1891, 3 November 1947.

sources.title: Nagar (princely state)
sources.note: Infobox c. 1300 to August 1972, 4,100 km2, tribute to the Kashmir Durbar to 1947, accession November 1947.

sources.title: Hunza-Nagar Campaign
sources.note: 1891 campaign dates and outcome; silent on the 1888 expulsion of the Dogras and on Kashmir's suzerainty.

sources.title: Gilgit-Baltistan
sources.note: Accession dates, 3 and 18 November 1947; abolition of Hunza September 1974; silent on Kashmir's suzerainty.

notes: No Cliopatria row. Two states on the pages (Hunza c. 1200, Nagar c. 1300) cited by four dossiers as one slug and one region (74.7 E, 36.35 N, 70 km); kept as one dossier with one disc. Vassal and tributary relations that other dossiers should carry, because the ledger types only record a state's own vassals: Hunza's tribute to China 'from around 1760' (the Qianlong Emperor recognised as suzerain, '1760 or 1761'), nominal allegiance to China 'from 1847' and tribute 'for the last time in 1938', tribute to the Dogras in 1860 'after their conquest of Gilgit' (Hunza page), Nagar's annual tribute to the Kashmir Durbar 'until 1947' (Nagar page), British suzerainty from 1891 (Gilgit-Baltistan page). The Kashmir and British Raj dossiers already carry the 1891 vassal_start; the Qing dossier, if it exists, lacks a Hunza vassal_start, and Kashmir has no 1860 event. Ruler tables on the pages overlap (Hunza: Mirza Khan 1790-1804 against Salim Khan III 1803-1825; Nagar: the table runs past the 1972 abolition), so no ruler strip. The Nagar infobox gives August 1972 as the end and the Hunza page 24 September 1974; the map ends the state at accession (November 1947) because the other dossiers hand the land to Pakistan then. Gazetteer names needed: Hunza, Nagar, Baltit/Karimabad. The Campaign page's infobox says both Mirs fled to China while the body says the Mir of Nagar stayed and was arrested. Wikidata id left null.
